the hygroscopicity measurements for KCl/WSOCs mixtures were compared with model predictions, and the discrepancies were found to be due to the formation and dissolution kinetics of potassium oxalate.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of organic compounds on the hygroscopicity and phase state of inorganic aerosols.
the hygroscopic properties of KCl/WSOCs mixtures and their implications in the formation of atmospheric particles.
the influence of biomass burning aerosols on the hygroscopic properties of atmospheric particles.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the hygroscopic behavior of KCl aerosol particles is significantly influenced by the presence of organic compounds, especially at high RH.
the water uptake behavior of aerosols is strongly affected by the presence of WSOCs.

the water uptake of KCl aerosols containing WSOCs is highly dependent on the composition and mixing state of aerosol particles, and the hygroscopic properties of KCl/WSOCs are more complicated than those predicted by the current model methods.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
water soluble organic compounds can influence hygroscopic behaviors in mixed aerosols and the effects depend on the organic compounds.
the hygroscopicity behavior of mixed particles is strongly dependent on the mixing ratios of organic and inorganic species and their interactions.
the water uptake behavior of KCl/WSOC mixtures is highly sensitive to the composition and mixing ratio of the organic compounds.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of organic compounds can significantly alter the hygroscopic properties of inorganic salts.

interactions between inorganic and organic species can significantly affect water uptake of aerosol particles, which can be a major factor in the prediction of hygroscopic growth of mixed atmospheric aerosols.

interactions between organic compounds and inorganic salt may lead to significant underestimation of water uptake by aerosol particles at intermediate RH, and thus should be taken into account when modeling water uptake and cloud condensation nuclei activity of atmospheric aerosols.
